proof_decision.trust_question: Do the Planning ownership repairs preserve truthful stacked-lane state, and does an unsynchronized source-checkout runtime fail with executable recovery before an unhandled dependency import?
proof_decision.narrowest_evidence: Eight existing focused scenarios pass: atomic lane creation/binding, explicit-lane new-plan reciprocal parent binding, supersede input ownership, current-work preservation, and lane-activation recovery. All 34 existing source-checkout launcher scenarios pass with the missing-dependency assertion folded into the two-checkout runtime-identity scenario. An isolated empty environment also returned typed `unsynchronized-source-runtime` JSON for missing `jsonschema`, exit 2, and a PowerShell-safe `uv sync --frozen --project ...` recovery. Ruff and generated command-package static/native Node proof pass.
proof_decision.prune_or_replacement_condition: Keep the transition-specific assertions in their existing owner tests and retain the combined two-checkout launcher scenario until runtime identity and dependency readiness are one typed pre-dispatch admission contract; do not add a separate fresh-worktree suite unless this focused boundary stops reproducing the ordinary path.
proof_decision.residual_risk: Hosted CI remains the cross-platform proof for generated adapters, uv behavior, and the stacked base. Broad affected suites were intentionally omitted locally under the repository test strategy because all changed semantics have focused existing owners.
